Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)
India's Maternal Health Cash Assistance Scheme, Explained Simply
A Public Awareness Reference Guide
1. Overview
Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) is a safe motherhood scheme run by the Government of India under the National Health Mission (NHM). It was launched in April 2005 by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. The scheme's main goal is to reduce deaths of mothers and newborns by encouraging pregnant women to deliver their babies in a hospital or health centre, with the help of trained doctors and nurses, instead of at home without medical support.
JSY does this by providing cash assistance directly to the mother when she delivers at a government hospital or an accredited private health facility. It also involves ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist) workers, who guide and support pregnant women through pregnancy check-ups, the delivery itself, and care afterward. JSY is implemented in every state and union territory, with extra focus on states that have historically had lower rates of hospital deliveries, known as Low Performing States (LPS).
2. Eligibility
Eligibility under JSY depends partly on where a woman lives and, in some cases, on her economic background:
In Low Performing States, all pregnant women delivering in a government or accredited private health facility are eligible for cash assistance, regardless of their age or how many children they already have.
In High Performing States, women from Below Poverty Line (BPL) households, and women belonging to Scheduled Castes (SC) or Scheduled Tribes (ST), are eligible for cash assistance for institutional delivery, generally up to two live births.
BPL pregnant women who prefer to deliver at home, rather than at a health facility, are also entitled to a smaller cash assistance, regardless of age or number of children.
Women choosing to deliver at an accredited private hospital are usually required to show valid BPL, SC, or ST proof, along with a referral from the ASHA worker, ANM, or medical officer.
Because eligibility rules can vary slightly depending on the state's classification and local guidelines, pregnant women and their families should confirm current criteria with their nearest ASHA worker, ANM, or health centre.
3. Benefits
JSY combines a cash incentive with supportive care during pregnancy, delivery, and after childbirth:
Cash Assistance for Institutional Delivery
* Low Performing States generally include states that have historically had lower institutional delivery rates; all other states and union territories are classified as High Performing States. Actual classification and amounts may be revised over time.
Other Benefits
A separate incentive is paid to the ASHA worker for accompanying and supporting the mother through antenatal check-ups and institutional delivery.
At least a minimum number of free antenatal check-ups are provided before delivery, along with a Mother and Child Protection Card and a JSY card to track entitlements.
JSY is closely linked with the Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK), which provides free delivery, free medicines, free diagnostic tests, free diet during the hospital stay, and free transport to and from the health facility, at no cost to the mother.
Cash assistance is generally transferred directly into the mother's bank account, so beneficiaries are encouraged to open a bank account, including through schemes like the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, if they do not already have one.
4. How to Apply
As soon as pregnancy is confirmed, register with the nearest Anganwadi Centre, Sub-Centre, or Primary Health Centre (PHC), ideally within the first few months. The local ASHA worker can help with this registration.
Complete the recommended antenatal check-ups and collect the Mother and Child Protection Card and JSY card issued by the ANM or ASHA worker; these track eligibility and entitlements through the pregnancy.
Provide bank account details and required identity documents, such as Aadhaar, so that the cash assistance can be transferred directly once the delivery is complete.
At the time of delivery, go to a government health facility or an accredited private hospital; the ASHA worker can help arrange transport and accompany the mother.
After delivery, ensure discharge documents and the JSY card are submitted at the health facility so that the cash assistance can be processed and credited to the bank account.
Families without easy access to these facilities, or with questions about their entitlement, can reach out to their ASHA worker, the nearest PHC or Sub-Centre, or call the NHM toll-free health helpline for guidance.
5. Source Basis
This document is based on general, publicly available information about the Janani Suraksha Yojana published by the National Health Mission (NHM) and the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW). No specific figures beyond those confirmed through official or reliable public sources have been included; all content has been rewritten in simple language. Cash assistance amounts and state classifications may be revised periodically, so readers should verify current details before applying.
National Health Mission (NHM), Government of India — Janani Suraksha Yojana — www.nhm.gov.in
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India (MoHFW) — www.mohfw.gov.in
National Health Mission, Odisha (Department of Health and Family Welfare, Government of Odisha) — www.nhmodisha.gov.in
